Question: Mr. \(A\) owns a home worth \(\$10{,}000.\) He sells it to Mr. \(B\) at a \(10\%\) profit based on the worth of the house. Mr. \(B\) sells the house back to Mr. \(A\) at a \(10\%\) loss. Then:
Solution:
Use the usual convention that \(B\)'s loss percentage is measured against his purchase price. Since \(A\) ends with the same house he started with, his gain is the cash received minus the cash paid to buy it back.

The first sale price, in dollars, is
\[
10{,}000+0.10(10{,}000)=11{,}000.
\]
Thus \(B\) paid $11,000. His \(10\%\) loss is based on this new amount, so he sells back for
\[
11{,}000-0.10(11{,}000)=9{,}900.
\]
After recovering his house, \(A\) retains \(11{,}000-9{,}900=\boxed{1{,}100}\) dollars. The answer is choice \(\boxed{B}\).
